messages.text: Verstappen usurps Russell in error-filled final practice ahead of 1pm Qualifying

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of fastest practice times as Red Bull led a renewed challenge to the Mercedes drivers ahead of Qualifying later on Friday at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Azerbaijan GP: Max Verstappen fastest in challenging final practice to usurp George Russell and Mercedes ahead of Qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Azerbaijan GP: Max Verstappen fastest in challenging final practice to usurp George Russell and Mercedes ahead of Qualifying Max Verstappen's pace suggests he could vie for Red Bull's first pole position of 2026; George Russell second, Lewis Hamilton third; watch Qualifying later on Friday at 1pm with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix itself on Saturday at 12pm, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Friday 25 September 2026 11:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell narrowly avoids hitting wall during the final practice session at the Azerbaijan GP. Max Verstappen denied George Russell a clean sweep of fastest practice times as Red Bull led a renewed challenge to the Mercedes drivers ahead of Qualifying later on Friday at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The arrival of more characteristic gusty conditions on the streets of Baku for final practice increased the challenge around the wall-lined circuit, with numerous drivers running off track after errors throughout the hour. Mercedes' dominance from Thursday's calmer running initially continued, but Verstappen found increasing pace on the soft tyres and eventually usurped Russell at the top of the timesheet with a best lap of 1:43.922. messages.text: Chelsea in landmark fertility policy: 'Being a player and mum are both possible now'

metadata.summary: Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health.
metadata.content: Chelsea Women: Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford discuss new fertility and player maternity policies in WSL first | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Chelsea Women: Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford discuss new fertility and player maternity policies in WSL first Chelsea are the first team in the WSL to introduce fertility and Player Maternity policies; it gives players the choice to have a family in whichever way they want to, with support during and after starting a family; Sonia Bompastor and Carly Telford explain more to Sky Sports Charlotte Marsh Senior Football Journalist Thursday 24 September 2026 16:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea have introduced fertility and player maternity policies which provide fully paid leave, personalised pregnancy support and dedicated return to play medical care Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health. Now, the Blues are the first team in the WSL to introduced new fertility and maternity policies, giving their players the choice to start a family in whichever way they want to, and the post-natal support to balance the demands of elite sport and motherhood. After World Cup heartbreak this summer they kick-off their Nations League campaign against Spain on Saturday at Wembley. The arrival of the world champions in the capital will be a painful reminder of what England were so close to achieving in North America - and re-exposes the scar, as boss Thomas Tuchel put it - of the mistakes made late on in that semi-final loss to Argentina. Tuchel has been eager to highlight the positives of England's campaign at the World Cup, insisting the experience and bonds built through the tournament leave the group well placed to kick on and achieve success in the Nations League and then at Euro 2028. messages.text: 'Exploitative ideas' - Top leagues criticise Infantino and call for FIFA reform

metadata.summary: A joint statement from Europe's top leagues has hit out at "exploitative ideas" pushed by FIFA president Gianni Infantino and called for "essential" reform of football's governing body.
metadata.content: FIFA: Gianni Infantino 'exploitative ideas' criticised as Premier League, Bundesliga, LaLiga and Serie A unite to call for reform | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content FIFA: Gianni Infantino 'exploitative ideas' criticised as Premier League, Bundesliga, LaLiga and Serie A unite to call for reform Europe's top leagues have released a statement calling for a shake-up of how FIFA is governed ahead of the March 2027 presidential elections; the top leagues in England, Germany, Spain and Italy have set out three core commitments they want the governing body to take up Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Friday 25 September 2026 10:05, UK Image: Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president appears precarious amid backlash to his World Cup sell-off plans A joint statement from Europe's top leagues has hit out at "exploitative ideas" pushed by FIFA president Gianni Infantino and called for "essential" reform of football's governing body. This summer, Infantino was forced to abandon a plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup after a backlash which led to UEFA pursuing legal action. Earlier this week, in a letter to FIFA members, Infantino said he was open to an independent external review of the plan and that he should be allowed to continue leading FIFA because his responsibilities are "larger than any individual proposal or disagreement". Havertz pulled up with the issue after a challenge from Quinten Timber in the first half of Thursday's 1-1 draw in Amsterdam and had to be substituted for Younes Ebnoutalib. metadata.content: Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz felt burnt out due to exposure before a lengthy layoff with a wrist injury | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Laver Cup: Carlos Alcaraz felt burnt out due to exposure before a lengthy layoff with a wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz reveals he "wants to miss tennis sometimes" after feeling burnt out from all his commitments before his injury lay-off; you can watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports Friday 25 September 2026 08:03, UK Image: Carlos Alcaraz felt physically and mentally exhausted before he suffered a wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April. The Spaniard, who won the Australian Open title at the start of the year, was forced to miss more than four months from tennis because of a right wrist injury . Alcaraz returned at the US Open where he reached the quarter-finals before losing a five-set thriller to American Ben Shelton , which finished at 3.33am local time.
